messages.subject: Identifying outlying loci
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,
I am trying to identify the outlying loci in my SNP data. I have used gl.outflank(gi, plot=True), which identified 10 loci with High Fst (below). Is there away to get the names of those 10 loci ?
$outflank$numberHighFstOutliers
[1] 10
Thanks heaps!
Robert

messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Identifying outlying loci
messages.body_plain:
Hi Robert,

If you run you command via:

out <- gl.outflank(possums.gl <http://possums.gl>)

then the

out$index that is returned has the information you need. This object is true if the snp is an outlier according to outflank.

So simply

locNames(possums.gl <http://possums.gl>)[out$index]

should give you the names of the loci.

Cheers, Bernd

messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Identifying outlying loci
messages.body_plain:
No if you want to know the most outlying ones you need to look into the out object that is returned. There for example you find the p values (or Fsts values of each loci) and then lowest(p) or highest Fsts are the most “outlying” ones.

So I would sort them and take say the 10 highest. Admittedly more than half is a lot.

In my data set I have normally around 5-10% of loci. How does your outflank plot look like?

Maybe your population structure is “funny”, hence the distribution of Fst values look strange.

Cheers, Bernd
